fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of travel on the street.
• Mark the location of the detached structure on any posted site map or address sign so arriving responders know a second building is on the property.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway and front entry area to maintain clear sightlines and overhead clearance for responding vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the sides of the walkway to keep the path clear for responder movement between structures.
• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing accessible from the front of the property to allow responders to reach the rear without circling the building.
• Post a notice at the front entry indicating that rear access is limited, so responders can plan accordingly on arrival.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored items that would block responders from staging or repositioning equipment near the front of the property.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and the detached structure to keep the path between buildings passable on foot.
• Mark any exterior utility shutoffs with visible, weather-resistant labels readable from a short distance.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches on large trees that hang directly over or close to the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the house.
• Separate scattered shrubs from the base of large trees to reduce connected plant material between ground level and tree canopies.
• Cut back any shrubs or low branches along the driveway to keep the travel path clear for vehicles.
• Keep the single access route free of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along its full length.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate quickly from the road.
• Thin scattered trees on the side of the property closest to the structure to widen the open area between the treeline and the house.
• Remove dead branches from large trees near the structure before they fall or carry fire upward.
• Keep the open green space mowed or cleared of tall dry grass that could carry fire toward the house.
